author: Niki Koswanage, Tom Redmond
description: Malaysian anti-corruption chief Azam Baki held millions of shares in a financial-services company, a corporate filing shows, the first public disclosure of a major stake in his name since an uproar over his shareholdings several years ago spurred protests calling for him to step down.
title: Malaysian Anti-Graft Chief Returns to Stock Market After Outcry

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Thomas Seal
description: President Donald Trump said he would start negotiations with Canada over a bridge project to connect Michigan and Ontario, threatening to block its opening until the US was given adequate compensation and owned “half of this asset.”
title: Trump Threatens to Block Detroit-Canada Bridge in New Trade Row

author: Eric Martin
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio will take part in Europe’s premier annual security conference and meetings with counterparts, just weeks after President Donald Trump’s desire to acquire Greenland generated alarm among US allies.
title: Rubio Heading to Munich for Security Forum After Greenland Alarm

author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump said his pick to lead the Federal Reserve can stoke the economy to grow at a rate of 15%, an exceedingly rosy target that nonetheless underscores the pressure that Kevin Warsh will face if confirmed to the role.
title: Trump Says Fed Pick Warsh Can Get US Economy to Hit 15% Growth

description: The Epstein files are threatening to bring down not the US president who was once his buddy, but a prime minister who never met the disgraced financier and sex trafficker. Tyler Kendall explains (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Starmer Never Knew Epstein. But He’s Becoming Collateral Damage.

author: Nasteho Said
description: Some 27 people were arrested in Sydney on Monday evening after police cracked down on protesters trying to move beyond a designated zone during demonstrations against the visit of Israeli President Isaac Herzog.
title: Australian Police Arrest 27 Protesting Israeli President’s Visit

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky, Eleanor Harrison-Dengate
description: On today’s Big Take podcast: As the US and Iran discuss another round of negotiations, Israel plans to meet with the US.
title: US and Iran Eye Talks as Netanyahu Heads to DC to Shape Strategy

author: Nathan R Dean
description: Amid Bitcoin’s volatility, the Trump-inspired rally evaporates.
title: What’s Next for the Cryptocurrency Rollercoaster?

author: Alex Wickham, Ellen Milligan, Joe Mayes
description: Keir Starmer shored up his position as UK prime minister during a dramatic day in Westminster that at times seemed like he might be forced to step down. The reprieve is likely only to be temporary.
title: Starmer Shores Up Position for Now as UK Rivals Bide Time

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss how Warsh's call for new Fed-Treasury accord unsettles bond market with Stuart Paul, Bloomberg Economics US and Canada Economist. They also discuss the additional pressure of treasuries as concerns that Chinese banks are reining in their holdings of US government bonds and questions over the health of the labor market with Citi Head of US Equity Trading Strategy, Stuart Kaiser. They also discuss Novo's escalation of the spat with Hims & Hers over the compounding pharmacy's obesity drug. Lastly, they check-in on the state of distressed real estate with Amy Rubenstein, Clear Investment Group CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Novo Sues Hims to Halt Obesity Drug Copycats | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 2/09/2026

author: Philip Aldrick
description: President Donald Trump’s trade wars are contributing to UK inflation as China raises prices on exports to Britain to recover the cost of US tariffs, Bank of England policymaker Catherine Mann said.
title: BOE’s Mann Says China Is Raising Export Prices Due to US Tariffs

author: William Horobin, Alessandra Migliaccio
description: President Emmanuel Macron has been handed a golden chance to insulate one of France’s most important institutions from the far right.
title: Macron Gifted a Chance to Start Making France More Le Pen-Proof

author: Zoe Tillman, Jimmy Jenkins
description: Federal prosecutors took steps to end a long-running criminal case against conservative activist Stephen Bannon, who had continued to challenge his conviction for defying a congressional subpoena after he served a four-month prison sentence.
title: DOJ Seeks to Drop 2021 Contempt Case Against Steve Bannon

description: Congress has less than five days for a bipartisan deal to avert yet another partial shutdown — and questions abound on what that would look like. Funding will lapse for the Department of Homeland Security Friday night unless Congressional Republicans, President Donald Trump and at least some Senate Democrats can find agreement on immigration enforcement. Or perhaps a plan to fund everything in the agency except ICE. Patrick McHenry, Former Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee, Former Speaker Pro Tempore, Bloomberg Contributor joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Shutdown Deadline Looms as Congress Reaches Homeland Impasse

description: Embattled United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer is being backed by his cabinet members as he faces more pressure to step down. Tyler Kendall has more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UK Cabinet Tries to Steady PM Starmer

description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit Washington on Wednesday to discuss US-Iran diplomacy with President Donald Trump, whose focus on Tehran’s nuclear program falls short of his ally’s call for more sweeping measures.  Natasha Hall, associate fellow at Chatham House, said President Trump's meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu may shape the US approach to negotiations with Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Netanyahu Hastens to Meet Trump Over Scope of Iran Diplomacy

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the upcoming Department of Homeland Security funding deadline. On today's show, Chatham House Associate Fellow Natasha Hall, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former Republican Congressman Patrick McHenry. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Homeland Security Funding Deadline Looms | Balance of Power: Early Edition 2/09/2026

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: The US is moving to reduce its so-called reciprocal tariff on goods from Bangladesh and offering a new exemption for textile products, the White House said Monday, in the latest adjustment for the South Asian country.
title: US Cuts Tariffs on Bangladesh Goods, Including Apparel Exception

author: Ani Avetisyan
description: US Vice President JD Vance signed a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Armenia on Monday, pledging as much as $9 billion in potential investment as the South Caucasus country seeks to reduce its long-standing reliance on Russia for energy.
title: US Pledges $9 Billion to Help Armenia Shift From Russian Energy

author: Andrea Jaramillo
description: Colombian prosecutors plan to charge Ecopetrol SA Chief Executive Officer Ricardo Roa over alleged violations of campaign spending limits in President Gustavo Petro’s 2022 presidential bid, El Tiempo reported.
title: Colombia Prosecutors Move to Charge Ecopetrol’s CEO Roa

author: Natalia Drozdiak
description: The Central Intelligence Agency is looking to speed up its access to breakthrough technologies in an effort to better compete with China.
title: CIA Looks to Speed Up Access to New Tech In Race Against China

author: Alex Wickham
description: The Epstein files are threatening to bring down not the US president who was once his buddy but a prime minister who never met the disgraced financier and sex trafficker.
title: Starmer Never Knew Epstein. But He’s Becoming Collateral Damage.

author: Brandon Sapienza
description: Staten Island’s status as a Republican stronghold in a city dominated by Democrats is under threat amid a Congressional redistricting fight
title: New York City Republicans Risk Losing Lone GOP Voice in Congress

description: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said lower US jobs numbers can be expected in the months ahead as population growth slows. The January jobs report is due out Wednesday. Luke Tilley of Wilmington Trust reacts on Bloomberg Surveillance. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: NEC's Hassett Warns of Weaker Jobs Report

author: Brandon Sapienza, Maya Davis
description: Thousands of New York City nurses reached a tentative labor agreement with local hospitals, putting an end in sight to a strike that’s stretched on for weeks.
title: New York Nurses Land Tentative Deal to End Weeks-Long Strike

author: Daniel Basteiro, Souhail Karam
description: The US said it convened rivals Morocco and Algeria for rare talks over the fate of the Western Sahara, as the Trump administration tries to resolve one of Africa’s longest-running territorial disputes.
title: US Convenes Foes Morocco, Algeria for Rare Western Sahara Talks

author: Patrick Van Oosterom
description: The new Dutch cabinet will include a swath of China hawks in the aftermath of a diplomatic crisis with Beijing over the ownership of Chinese chipmaker Nexperia.
title: China Critics Shape New Dutch Cabinet After Chipmaker Row

author: Alberto Nardelli, Andrea Palasciano
description: The European Union is preparing a series of options to embed Ukraine’s membership in a future peace deal, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: EU Is Readying Options to Give Ukraine Gradual Membership Rights

description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is edging closer to the exit — and now the pressure is growing from inside his own party. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Will Starmer Resign? PM Clings to Power

author: Nduka Orjinmo
description: Nigerian protesters marched to the National Assembly on Monday to voice their anger at legislators approving changes to electoral laws, while omitting a key reform demanded by the opposition.
title: Nigerian Protesters Want Election Results Uploaded in Real Time

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: Spanish train drivers called off a planned three-day strike after unions reached a deal with the government, following calls for change after two deadly accidents in January.
title: Spanish Train Drivers Call Off Three-Day Strike

description: Takaichi called a snap election expecting a risk. Instead, it strengthened her position in Parliament. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Gearoid Reidy explains what the result means for her agenda and Japan’s politics. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Takaichi’s Election Gamble Paid Off

author: Jamie Tarabay
description: Ghislaine Maxwell, the convicted accomplice of disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein refused on Monday to answer any questions from a House panel investigating Epstein’s sex-trafficking operation.
title: Maxwell Invokes Right to Silence on Lawmakers’ Epstein Questions

author: Gregory Korte
description: President Donald Trump’s call for Republicans to “nationalize” voting rules has revived a long-running constitutional debate over how much influence the federal government should have in US elections.
title: How Trump’s Call to ‘Nationalize’ Elections Runs Into the Constitution

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: An unexpected election victory for the pro-royalist Bhumjaithai Party led by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is set to bring some stability to Thailand following years of political upheaval that left its economy adrift.
title: What Next for Thailand After Anutin’s Surprise Election Win?

author: Courtney McBride, Ben Bartenstein
description: The US said in an advisory that American-flagged ships should stay as far as possible from Iranian waters when navigating the Strait of Hormuz after a vessel was harassed last week, with tensions remaining high between Washington and Tehran.
title: US Tells American Ships to Keep Away From Iran Amid Tensions

author: Alex Morales
description: Scottish Labour Leader Anas Sarwar urged UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to quit his post over his controversial appointment of Peter Mandelson as US ambassador, becoming the most senior party figure so far to pull support from the beleaguered premier.
title: Scottish Labour Leader Calls on Starmer to Quit Over Mandelson

author: Michelle Kaske
description: New Jersey Transit suspended rail service Monday between New York’s Penn Station and Trenton, while Amtrak canceled some trains between Philadelphia and New York City, the passenger-rail providers said, citing a downed overhead wire.
title: NJ Transit Suspends Service Between New York City and Trenton

author: William Horobin
description: Bank of France Governor Francois Villeroy de Galhau unexpectedly quit early in a move that leaves the choice of his successor to Emmanuel Macron instead of a possible future president from the far right.
title: Villeroy Quits Bank of France, Letting Macron Pick Governor

description: Vikas Dwivedi, energy strategist at Macquarie, discusses the outlook for oil prices and what he calls a "looming risk" of supply disruptions even as tensions in the Middle East eased . He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hard to Short Oil Due to 'Looming Risk,' Macquarie Says

author: Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer pledged to press on with his agenda as the departure of a second senior aide in 24 hours left the UK prime minister’s grip on power appearing increasingly tenuous.
title: Starmer Vows to Fight On as UK PM as Second Top Aide Quits

description: Chinese regulators have advised financial institutions to rein in their holdings of US Treasuries, citing concerns over concentration risks and market volatility, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Ven Ram reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: China Warns Banks to Rein in Holdings of US Treasuries

author: Jan Bratanic
description: Slovenian opposition leader Janez Jansa extended his lead over Prime Minister Robert Golob’s center-left party less than six weeks ahead of a parliamentary election, boosting the chances that the Donald Trump-aligned nationalist may return to power.
title: Slovenia Opposition Extends Poll Lead Six Weeks Before Election

author: Alastair Gale
description: Japan’s prime minister Sanae Takaichi just scored the biggest electoral victory of the postwar period.
title: Japanese Voters Empower Takaichi to Fight Tokyo’s Corner

author: Golnar Motevalli
description: Iran extended the prison sentence of a Nobel peace laureate and detained several prominent reformist figures, escalating a crackdown on dissents weeks after security forces killed thousands of people to quell nationwide protests.
title: Iran Hardens Crackdown on Political Dissidents After US Talks

author: Jim Wyss
description: La política de la isla está más arraigada, por lo que es probable que la estrategia que EE.UU. utilizó en Venezuela no funcione.
title: Élite cubana en Miami sueña con reconstruir Cuba pero teme que ya sea demasiado tarde

author: Jim Wyss
description: The regime is so entrenched that the playbook the US used in Venezuela isn't likely to work on the island.
title: Miami Elites Who Dream of Rebuilding Cuba Fear It’s Too Far Gone

description: European Union Competition Commissioner Teresa Ribera discusses the EU's warning given to Meta Platforms Inc. over policies that block the use of rival Artificial Intelligence assistants on WhatsApp, raising the possibility of further tensions with the Trump administration over the regulation of US tech companies. Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Ribera also comments on Google's ad tech business and Netflix and Paramount’s battle over Warner Bros. Discovery. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: EU Says Meta Warning Is About Protecting Consumers

author: Laura Dhillon Kane
description: Mark Carney has promised to spend big on defense. Canadian technology companies sense opportunity.
title: Canada’s Race to Rebuild Military Triggers a Defense-Tech Gold Rush

author: Alastair Gale, Jing Li
description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s election victory is handing Chinese leader Xi Jinping a dilemma: Engage with Japan’s most popular post-war leader or continue a deep freeze with the US’s top ally in Asia.
title: Xi Faces Dilemma Over Japan After Takaichi Wins Historic Mandate

description:
An election night surprise in Thailand. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s party is outperforming expectations, riding incumbency and a nationalist surge after border tensions with Cambodia.



 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stability Drives Thailand’s Election Surprise

author: Rakesh Sharma
description: Indian Oil Corp. and Hindustan Petroleum Corp. jointly bought a cargo of Venezuelan crude, marking a second deal on the trade by the nation’s processors after Reliance Industries Ltd. snapped up a shipment.
title: More Indian Refiners Take Venezuelan Oil as US Reshapes Flows

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, the Nikkei 225 soared, leading Asia higher, after Sanae Takaichi’s historic election victory.

Keir Starmer is facing a battle for political survival after his top aide quit amid the controversy over former US envoy Peter Mandelson’s appointment.

Bloomberg understands that Chinese regulators have advised banks to limit their exposure to US Treasuries, citing concerns over market volatility and concentration risks.

Today's guests: Economist and Currency Strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia Carol Kong & Reform UK Deputy Leader, Richard Tice (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Takaichi's Landslide Win & Starmer On The Brink as Key Aide Quits | Daybreak Europe 2/9/2026

author: Alice Atkins
description: UK government bonds and the pound are coming under pressure as Keir Starmer attempts to rescue his premiership and rattled investors brace for another round of political instability.
title: Gilts, Pound on Edge as Doubts on Keir Starmer’s Future Grow

author: Faris Mokhtar
description: Singapore’s income inequality fell to a record low last year amid lingering cost-of-living concerns, with Prime Minister Lawrence Wong pledging to reduce the gap further.
title: Singapore’s Income Inequality at Record Low But Concerns Linger

author: Rakesh Sharma
description: India’s imports of Russian oil are expected to drop by about half from already weaker recent levels, according to people with direct knowledge of the purchases, after US President Donald Trump issued an order detailing some terms of a trade deal between the two nations.
title: Indian Imports of Russian Oil Seen Halving on US Order

description: The pound fell to the lowest in two weeks versus the euro and the dollar on Feb. 5 on concerns around Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s grasp on power and as the Bank of England came within one vote of cutting interest rates. Paul Jackson, strategist at Invesco Asset Management, says overall he's positive on UK assets and that "throughout the year sterling can appreciate a bit against the dollar." He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Bearish Pound Bets Increase as PM Starmer Teeters

author: Yian Lee
description: Chinese military flights into a sensitive area near Taiwan in January fell to the lowest level of Lai Ching-te’s presidency, an indication it is tweaking its training focus.
title: China Sends Fewer Flights Near Taiwan in Sign of Training Shift

author: John Cheng
description: Investor reaction to Japan’s election signals at least a temporary reprieve for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi from market ructions that have threatened to undermine her spending plans.
title: Markets Give Takaichi Benefit of Doubt as Stocks, Yen Climb

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon, Neil Jerome Morales
description: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte is facing her third impeachment complaint as critics revived efforts to remove her from office, days after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. survived attempts to oust him.
title: Philippines VP Duterte Faces Third Impeachment Complaint

author: Andra Timu, Piotr Skolimowski
description: Romania’s finance chief said winning back investor confidence by trimming the nation’s outsized budget deficit should amount to a “national project” as the government struggles to wrest control over fiscal policy.
title: Romania Says Budget Agenda Aims to Bring Debt Costs Below 6%

author: Stephen Wicary, Dina Khrennikova
description: Cuba is at risk of losing vital airline service as it prepares to run out of aviation fuel, while an allied nation cut off an important escape valve for migrants amid increasing pressure from the US aimed at toppling the regime in Havana.
title: Cuba Warns Airlines They Can’t Refuel After Trump Tariff Threat

author: Nectar Gan, Shawna Kwan, Laura Davison
description: A Hong Kong court sentenced former media mogul Jimmy Lai to 20 years in prison, handing the pro-democracy activist the heaviest penalty yet meted out under a 2020 Beijing-imposed national security law.
title: Jimmy Lai’s 20-Year Term Seals China’s Move to Muzzle Critic
